subject: Private VPC deployment follow-up: networking details & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-18T15:02:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: Private VPC deployment — networking questions and next steps

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a few clarifying questions so our solutions team can size the Private deployment correctly. Top-level we heard that Acme prefers a Private VPC deployment (not Hosted or Dedicated) due to regulatory data controls and network isolation. Confirming our understanding and next steps below.

Summary of choices we discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest to deploy, but data would transit our hosted control plane — not preferred given your requirements.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools in our infra with logical isolation — good for predictable throughput but still runs in Redwood-managed VPCs.
- Private VPC (your preference): customer-managed VPC with PrivateLink or VPC peering to connect runtime. This supports stricter egress/ingress controls and onboarded KMS.

Networking details we need to confirm from your side (please share with your cloud/network team):
1) Preferred connectivity: AWS PrivateLink (Endpoint Service) or VPC Peering?
2) VPC CIDR(s) for the subnets you expect us to peer with (please include primary and any cross-account CIDRs).
3) Any IP allowlist requirements for management/control-plane traffic (we can provide endpoint IP ranges).
4) Are there forced egress NAT gateways or strict egress filtering that will block our runtime outbound calls (for updates/metrics)?
5) TLS termination: will you accept our certs via PrivateLink, or do you require customer-managed certs/ALB in front?
6) KMS/HSM: do you want Redwood to integrate with your KMS for encryption keys? If yes, which IAM role/policies should we expect?
7) Cross-region considerations: which AWS region(s) should the runtime be deployed into?

Attachments I’m sending: redwood-network-checklist.pdf (short checklist for your network team), and a template spreadsheet to capture VPC CIDRs.

Next steps we propose:
- You: share a network contact and the answers to the questions above (or permission to loop them into this thread).
- Redwood: schedule a 60-minute technical call with our infra engineer (Dev) and architect (Vivek) once we have the network details.
- Procurement: we’ll send a preliminary SOW and deployment timeline after the technical call.

Would Monday or Tuesday next week work for the technical call? I can block options.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0127

Attachments: redwood-network-checklist.pdf (network checklist, 2 pages); acme-vpc-cidr.xlsx (template for CIDRs and contact details)
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-18T17:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC deployment — networking questions and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and aligns with what we discussed. Quick answers (high-level) from our side:

1) We'd prefer VPC Peering initially for simplicity; looking to evaluate PrivateLink later for cross-account controls.
2) Primary VPC CIDR: 10.10.0.0/16 (prod). Secondary: 10.20.0.0/16 (staging). We will share the full spreadsheet with subnet ranges.
3) IP allowlist: procurement wants control-plane traffic restricted to our management subnets (10.10.100.0/24). Is it possible to provide a short list of control-plane IPs?
4) Egress: we have restrictive egress via NAT gateway; outbound to service endpoints must be whitelisted. We can open necessary endpoints once you provide them.
5) TLS: we prefer customer-managed certs on an ALB in front of the endpoint. Happy to provide certs via ACM.
6) KMS: yes, we want keys in our account. Happy to provide cross-account role for key usage.
7) Region: us-west-2 for prod initially.

Network contact: Sarah Nguyen (sarah.nguyen@acme-analytics.com), Cloud Network Lead. I’ll loop her in. Procurement is CC’d on this reply.

Regarding timeline: target Q3 pilot in prod with a limited workload. Procurement will need the SOW + security questionnaire.

— Jordan

On Fri, Jun 18, 2026 at 15:02 Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> [original message above]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-analytics.com>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-06-19T09:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC deployment — networking questions and next steps

Thanks Jordan — and hi Sarah, great to e-meet you. I’ve attached the redwood-network-checklist.pdf and the CIDR template; please populate and send back when convenient.

Quick clarifications from our infra side:
- For VPC Peering we’ll need the peering connection to be created from your account and accepted by our runtime account; we can provide the peer-account ID and exact VPC ID once the SOW is in place.
- Control-plane IPs: we can provide a short-lived set of IP ranges for the control-plane endpoints. If you prefer DNS-based allowlisting via PrivateLink that’s also supported.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys. We will need an IAM role that allows Redwood's runtime account to use the key (we can share the role ARN and required policy).
- Certificates: ALB with ACM works — we’ll support that flow and can validate the ACM cert via DNS/ACM methods.

Proposed next steps:
1) Sarah: please fill the CIDR template and confirm whether you prefer VPC Peering or PrivateLink for production.
2) Once we have the completed sheet, Dev and Vivek will propose a 60-minute engineer-to-engineer call (I’m suggesting Tue or Wed next week).
3) Procurement: Marissa will send a preliminary SOW and security docs (SOC 2, data flow diagrams) within 48 hours of the technical call.

I’ll tentatively propose Tue 2026-06-23 09:00 PT / Wed 2026-06-24 10:00 PT for the technical call — Sarah/Vivek/Dev please confirm.

Thanks —
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — Sarah filled out the spreadsheet and prefers VPC Peering for now. She also included subnet ranges and a direct contact number. We’re good to move forward with the engineer call; Tue 2026-06-23 09:00 PT works for our team.

Procurement asked for a draft SOW and the initial security packet (SOC 2 + data flow). Can you send that after the call?

I’ll await the calendar invite.

— Jordan
